name: Influenza (flu)
summary: Seasonal vaccines that protect against influenza, generally recommended for people aged six months and older.
descriptionParagraphs: Influenza is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. CDC recommends seasonal flu vaccination for most people aged six months and older, with some products limited to particular age groups or health histories.

Flu vaccines come as inactivated, recombinant or live attenuated products. Most are given by injection; an eligible nasal-spray formulation is also available. Some children need two doses in a season. Confirm the right product and timing with a qualified provider.
ageGroup: Generally people aged 6 months and older, with product-specific restrictions
vaccineType: Inactivated, recombinant or live attenuated, depending on product
administrationMethod: Injection, or an eligible nasal-spray formulation
scheduleSummary: Seasonal vaccination; number of doses depends on age and vaccination history

name: COVID-19
summary: Vaccines that protect against COVID-19; CDC recommends them for people aged 6 months and older through individual decision-making with a provider.
descriptionParagraphs: COVID-19 is a respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. CDC recommends the current season's COVID-19 vaccine for people aged 6 months and older, based on individual decision-making with a provider, and describes it as especially important for people aged 65 and older, people at high risk for severe COVID-19 and people who have never been vaccinated. CDC updates this guidance for each season.

Products in the United States are either mRNA or protein subunit vaccines, and all are given by injection. Because the schedule changes over time, VaxAccess does not publish a fixed seasonal schedule; follow CDC's current guidance and confirm with a qualified provider.

name: Mpox
summary: Vaccination for people who meet mpox exposure or risk criteria; the documented Austin clinic used the two-dose JYNNEOS vaccine.
descriptionParagraphs: Mpox is a viral disease. CDC recommends vaccination for people who meet its exposure or risk criteria, and advises that vaccinated people should still avoid close, skin-to-skin contact with someone who has mpox. Use in people younger than 18 requires review by a provider.

The Austin clinic documented on this site used JYNNEOS, a live, nonreplicating vaccine. It is given by subcutaneous injection or, where eligible, intradermal injection; people younger than 18 receive it subcutaneously. CDC recommends two doses, the second four weeks (28 days) after the first. Confirm eligibility and timing with a qualified provider.
ageGroup: People meeting exposure or risk criteria; age-specific use requires provider review
vaccineType: Live, nonreplicating (JYNNEOS, used at the documented event)
scheduleSummary: Two doses, four weeks (28 days) apart
